newsitem.title: UK: BA cabin crew vote for three-day strikes.
newsitem.headline: BA cabin crew vote for three-day strikes.

text.p: Cabin crew at British Airways on Monday night voted in favour of a series of three-day strikes in their five-month-old dispute over pay and conditions.

The result of the vote, held at a meeting between cabin crew and their union the Transport and General Workers Union (T & G) at London's Heathrow airport, will be put to the union's general secretary, Bill Morris, on Tuesday.

"The meeting made a recommendation that they go for a series of 72-hour disputes. That will be relayed to General Secretary Bill Morris who will authorise it,"T & G spokesman George Ryde told reporters.
If Morris approves the action, he will set the date for the first strike, Ryde said.

Cabin crew voted by a margin of two-to-one last week in favour of strikes, while the airline's ground staff voted earlier on Monday to hold a separate strike in protest at BA's planned sale of its catering unit.

The threatened strikes have made it likely that BA flights will be seriously disrupted. However, the T & G's Morris has written to BA's chief executive Robert Ayling offering peace talks in the dispute with the ground staff.

Ayling welcomed the T&G's peace move and said he was ready to start discussions immediately. "Talks will happen as far as I'm concerned, and my managers are ready now. I can't see why we can't have an agreement very quickly," he told a news conference.
BA is trying to save one billion pounds ($1.7 billion) by 2000 in a cost-cutting drive and the squeeze has put it into conflict with the unions.
It has, in the meantime, drawn up a battle-plan to keep services flying.

All management have been re-trained to allow them to take on more roles, extra security will be brought in to get strike breakers through picket-lines and the group is also willing to hire external staff to take on BA strikers' jobs.

The airline, fresh from a 60 million pound facelift and in the midst of seeking regulatory clearance for its alliance with AMR Corp's American Airlines, has placed all operations on red alert to combat the strike threat.
